questions.q: Let R be the relation on the integers defined by a R b if and only if 5 divides (a - b). Prove that R is an equivalence relation and describe its equivalence classes.
questions.model: Reflexive: a - a = 0 is divisible by 5. Symmetric: 5 | (a - b) implies 5 | (b - a). Transitive: 5 | (a - b) and 5 | (b - c) imply 5 | (a - c) = (a - b) + (b - c). Classes: [0], [1], [2], [3], [4], the residues modulo 5.

questions.q: R = {(1,2), (2,3), (3,4)} is a relation on {1, 2, 3, 4}. How many ordered pairs does the transitive closure of R contain?
True or False: The set {1, 2, 3, 6, 12, 18} partially ordered by divisibility is a lattice.
questions.model: False. 12 and 18 have common multiples only outside the set (36), so they have no least upper bound in the set.

questions.q: Let f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = x^2 on the real numbers. Find the value of (f o g)(2), where (f o g)(x) = f(g(x)).

opts: Reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
questions.model: It is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, hence an equivalence relation (classes {1,2} and {3}).

questions.q: Two fair dice are rolled. Given that the first die shows an even number, what is the probability that the sum is 8? Give the answer as a decimal.
questions.model: Outcomes with the first die even: 18. Of these, sum 8: (2,6), (4,4), (6,2), 3 outcomes. P = 3/18 = 1/6 = 0.1667.

questions.q: Each item from a machine is defective with probability 0.1, independently. In a sample of 5 items, what is the probability that exactly 2 are defective?

questions.t: expected values, mean, variance and standard deviation
questions.q: A random variable X takes the values 0, 1 and 2 with probabilities 0.2, 0.5 and 0.3. Find the variance of X.
Explain when the Poisson distribution is a good approximation to the binomial distribution, and give its parameter in terms of n and p.
questions.model: When n is large and p is small (rare events) with np moderate; the Poisson parameter is lambda = np, and P(X = k) = e^(-lambda) lambda^k / k!.

questions.q: Construct the truth table of (p -> q) AND (q -> p) and show that it is logically equivalent to p <-> q.
questions.model: Rows (p,q): TT -> T, TF -> F, FT -> F, FF -> T for both expressions, so the columns are identical and the statements are equivalent.

questions.q: Using the laws of logic, show that NOT (p OR (NOT p AND q)) is logically equivalent to NOT p AND NOT q, naming the law used at each step.
questions.model: NOT(p OR (NOT p AND q)) = NOT p AND NOT(NOT p AND q) [De Morgan] = NOT p AND (p OR NOT q) [De Morgan, double negation] = (NOT p AND p) OR (NOT p AND NOT q) [distributive] = F OR (NOT p AND NOT q) [negation law] = NOT p AND NOT q [identity].

questions.q: 'If it rains, the match is cancelled. The match was not cancelled. Therefore it did not rain.' Which rule of inference is used?
questions.model: From p -> q and NOT q, conclude NOT p: modus tollens.

questions.q: Prove by mathematical induction that 3 divides n^3 - n for every integer n >= 1.
questions.model: Base: n = 1 gives 0, divisible by 3. Step: assume 3 | k^3 - k. Then (k+1)^3 - (k+1) = (k^3 - k) + 3k^2 + 3k, a sum of multiples of 3, so 3 divides it. Hence true for all n >= 1.

questions.q: By Lagrange's theorem, which of the following cannot be the order of a subgroup of a group of order 12?
questions.model: The order of a subgroup divides the order of the group; 5 does not divide 12.

What is the minimum number of students in a class that guarantees at least 3 of them were born in the same month?
questions.model: Generalised pigeonhole: 2 x 12 + 1 = 25.

questions.q: Solve the recurrence a(n) = 5a(n-1) - 6a(n-2) with a(0) = 1 and a(1) = 4, and use your solution to find a(4).
questions.model: Characteristic equation r^2 - 5r + 6 = 0, roots 2 and 3: a(n) = A 2^n + B 3^n. A + B = 1, 2A + 3B = 4 give B = 2, A = -1. a(n) = 2 x 3^n - 2^n; a(4) = 162 - 16 = 146.

questions.q: Read the assertion and reason about euler and Hamilton paths and choose the correct option.
questions.assertion: The complete graph K4 has no Euler circuit.
questions.reason: Every vertex of K4 has odd degree.
questions.model: A connected graph has an Euler circuit iff every vertex has even degree; in K4 each vertex has degree 3, so both are true and R explains A.

questions.q: G1 is the cycle on 6 vertices and G2 consists of two disjoint triangles. Both have 6 vertices, 6 edges and every vertex of degree 2. Are they isomorphic? Justify using a graph invariant.
questions.model: No. Isomorphism preserves connectivity (and cycle lengths); G1 is connected with a 6-cycle, G2 has two components and only 3-cycles.

questions.q: Model the case as a rooted tree, state the tree properties you rely on, and design a traversal that computes the total size of every folder. Justify the traversal order you choose.
questions.case: A storage server holds a folder hierarchy: each folder can contain files (with sizes) and sub-folders, and there are no links between folders. The administrator needs the total size of every folder, including everything inside its sub-folders.
questions.model: Folders and files are vertices, containment edges; with no cross links it is a tree (connected, acyclic, n vertices and n - 1 edges, unique path from the root). A postorder traversal computes each child's total before its parent, so a folder's size = own files + sum of sub-folder totals, in O(n) time.
